answer: Ten thousand ballots from three cloud data centers form a nebula around one center — a sybil farm's shape. Each ballot must arrive from its own autonomous system — a distinct ASN with an RPKI-signed route live in the public BGP table of 125,670 networks for 30 days — and no ASN may carry more than 25 ballots. A farm cramming 10,000 ballots into three cloud ASNs dies at that summit: 9,925 are thrown out at once, before voting. Spreading legally costs real money: 400 ASNs need 400 leased /24 blocks at $102 a month each, $40,800 monthly — and one jade seal cannot stamp a thousand ballots.
